title: The Tap of a Cane
story:
Dawn came slowly to Oakhaven, painting the cold stone of the Grand Library in pale, golden light. From his high stone alcove, James watched the shadows retreat. He held the green sea-glass to his eye, turning the golden city into a familiar, emerald world. He thought of the quiet depth of the Great Canopy. He thought of the steady drift of Silas's canal barge. He thought of the warm, ticking comfort of the clockmaker’s hearth.

The streets below began to stir with the quiet murmurs of early morning. A distant motor-carriage rumbled, its metallic scent drifting up the steps, but James did not shrink back today. He felt the weight of the brass canister against his shoulder, a solid anchor in this world of stone and iron. He was no longer just a visitor passing through; he had a map, he had a path, and he had a destination.

A rhythmic sound echoed up the grand staircase—not the heavy clatter of work boots or the rolling of iron wheels, but the steady, comforting tap-tap-tap of a walking cane. James peered over the ledge. Climbing the steps with a slow but determined pace was Barnaby. The old man paused to catch his breath, looking up toward the grand doors, when his eyes caught the small figure perched in the alcove.

A warm, familiar smile creaked across the old man's face, and he raised his hand in a quiet greeting. James scrambled down from his perch, his leather strap bouncing against his side. As they stood together before the towering wooden doors, this man reached into his pocket and produced a heavy brass key, unlocking the small side entrance with a reassuring wink. The doors groaned inward, revealing a cavernous hall smelling of old paper, leather, and endless mystery.
location: The entrance hall of the Grand Library
